raw: {"need": "Competence", "secondary": {"name": "Autonomy"}, "read": "The stalling is almost never about laziness; it is about not wanting to start something that might prove they cannot do it. The desk becomes a place where their ability gets tested, and the morning drag is the brain buying time before that test begins. I actually think the stalling is telling me something real, and I would rather know what that is than just keep pushing."}, {"phase": "Curiosity", "words": "When you sit down and then kind of drift, what is going through your head right then? Is it that you do not know where to start, that it feels like a lot, that it just feels pointless? I am genuinely asking, not setting you up."}, {"phase": "Collaboration", "words": "So here is what I want to try. The work stays, but the shape of it is something we can build together."}, {"phase": "Commitment", "words": "I am holding you to doing the work every day because I know you are more than capable of it, and I am not willing to let you talk yourself out of proving that. situation: My kid stalls every morning on the schoolwork we agreed to.
